description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:1296-1314 (handle_space_join invite-code branch).

The comparison uses subtle::ConstantTimeEq::ct_eq on the invite-code bytes:
    .find(|inv| inv.code.as_bytes().ct_eq(code.as_bytes()).into())

This is correct: invite codes are CSPRNG-derived credentials (16-byte / 32-hex), and a plain == short-circuits at first mismatched byte, exposing a byte-by-byte timing oracle.

What a future contributor might suggest changing:
- 'Use Iterator::find with == — the codes are short, the timing leak is theoretical.' False: the linear-scan find is repeatedly called per byte for an attacker, and aggregating timing differences over many requests recovers the code. This pattern has been demonstrated in real attacks against MAC/token comparisons.
- 'Move the compare into the backend — it's storage-layer business.' Possible refactor, but the kit owns the invite-redemption logic today; moving the compare into the backend means trusting that every future backend implementor also uses ct_eq. The current placement is defense-in-depth.
- 'Eliminate the linear scan — the backend should provide find_by_code.' True (and the same point as the architectural fix in JMAP-x2gd.10), but the inner compare must remain ct_eq.

The doc-comment at 1300-1310 captures why this matters (length-discrimination note plus the cit to bd:JMAP-sc1b.89). Preserve both the choice and the comment.
title: Constant-time invite code compare in handle_space_join is correct and load-bearing
